title: Winding number and circular coloring
summary: In 1996, Youngs proved a surprising theorem that quadrangulations of the projective plane could never have chromatic number exactly 3. This sparked a lot of interest, and the result has been further developed in many directions over the past decades. For example, the result is strengthened by considering the circular chromatic number, which is a real-valued lower bound on the chromatic number. The circular chromatic number of a quadrangulation cannot be in the interval (2,4). This parameter allows a generalization to larger even faces, for which a similar gap exists.
